title: Routing and isochrones
text: Often best route simply fastest one: dispatcher may want keep trucks residential streets, cyclist may want stay . ox_add_edge_penalties() turns preference per-edge column — , metres edge spends calm residential road classes: soft version just folds penalty routing weight (ordinary shortest path trades seconds residential metres fixed rate). interesting questions, though, hard: fastest route using budget residential metres, whole trade-curve look like? ox_route_pareto() answers second — enumerates every Pareto-optimal route exactly (bicriteria label-setting Rust core; one-way streets respected): successive route little slower little calmer; route beats criteria. Plotted, alternatives fan fast arterial option quiet residential one:  ox_route_constrained() answers first question — exact constrained shortest path one chosen budget: metro-sized networks enumerating exact front gets expensive, ox_route_constrained(..., method = "lagrangian") solves problem Lagrangian relaxation — handful plain Dijkstra runs — returning feasible route together proven lower bound optimal cost (message reports duality gap whenever optimality certified). title: osmnxr 0.1.6
text: parity pass OSMnx gained 2025–2026 (releases 2.0.1–2.1.1), plus OSMnx 2.0 features simplification/consolidation step missing. Rust core now crate . graph algorithms (CSR graph, Dijkstra, Yen, Pareto/constrained routing, TSP, centrality, simplification, snapping) moved unchanged dependency-free crate osmnxr-core (https://strategicprojects.github.io/osmnxr-core/), package pins exactly bundles src/rust/vendor.tar.xz; src/rust/src/lib.rs keeps extendr wrappers. Results change. Building source needs Rust 1.81 later. Overpass network filters now mirror OSMnx 2.1’s tag tag, replacing simplified highway-regexes used far. Downloads gain negative filters (area=yes, access=private, motor_vehicle=, foot=, bicycle=, service-road subtypes, ways tagged rest_area/services, walk ways whose sidewalk mapped separate way), two network types join drive/walk/bike/: drive_service (drivable including service roads) all_public. Note two behaviour changes: "drive" longer includes service roads (use "drive_service"), "" now means every -use way including private access rather literally every highway value. ox_simplify() now preserves every edge attribute column (merged edge takes first segment’s value) instead keeping highway name, gained edge_attr_aggs (OSMnx 2): named list functions combining per-segment values along merged chain, e.g. list(travel_time = sum, speed_kph = mean). default travel_time penalty summed present, pre-computed routing weights survive simplification instead dropped. ox_consolidate_intersections() accepts per-node tolerance (one merge radius per node, OSMnx 2: nodes merge buffers tolerance/2 overlap), validates tolerance, now warns asked consolidate already-consolidated graph — proceeds, since re-clustering larger tolerance well-defined , double run made visible. New ox_validate() checks graph meets package’s structural expectations — sf types, complete unique node ids, resolvable u/v, usable length, one CRS, edge geometries actually run u node v node — reporting every problem found one pass (OSMnx gained validation helpers 2.1.0). Handy building layer hand ox_blend()/ox_union().

title: osmnxr 0.1.5
text: New ox_blend() blends point locations — whole second graph — street network (#6, requested @talegari), osmnxr counterpart sfnetworks::st_network_blend(): point snapped onto nearest edge (grid-indexed planar search Rust core) edge split , directions two-way street, turning location routable node. Attributes preserved (length recomputed; travel_time / penalty rescaled proportionally), points beyond tolerance skipped warning, meta$blend maps every input node. Given second osm_graph, three-step recipe issue applied: blend nodes , stack graphs ox_union(), add connector edges snapped pair — one routable multimodal network. ox_blend() gained finer control @talegari’s field test Delhi road + metro networks (#6): meta$blend now also records u / v, endpoints edge point snapped onto; snap_nodes flags points (y nodes) may snap (station gates yes, platforms ); snap_edges flags edges g may receive (keep limited-access flyovers); connector_node_attrs copies y node attributes — say, per-station access time — onto connector edges; reusing g osmid y different coordinates now error renumbering hint, instead silently corrupting first-wins merge. New ox_route_shortest() rounds ox_route_* family (#5 feedback, @talegari): sf interface shortest-path routing, returning cost, node path merged street geometry per route, k > 1 enumerating loopless alternatives (Yen) — one naming scheme one return shape across ox_route_shortest(), ox_route_constrained(), ox_route_pareto() ox_route_tsp(). ox_shortest_path() ox_k_shortest_paths() remain lighter node-sequence variants. Repeated routing calls graph much faster (#5 feedback, @talegari): structural edge index every router marshals Rust core (dominant per-call cost metro-sized graphs) now cached session, content-addressed graph’s node ids edge endpoints — copies hit, edits miss, nothing goes stale. NCR Delhi network (2.1M directed edges) warm ox_route_constrained() call drops ~0.7 s Rust solve time . ox_clear_cache() also clears cache. Dijkstra/Yen solvers additionally return edges traversed, ox_route_shortest() ox_route_tsp() draw exact geometry across parallel edges (previously ox_route_tsp() drew minimum-weight twin). New preference-aware routing (#5, requested @talegari): ox_route_constrained() finds exact minimum-cost route whose consumption second edge criterion stays within budget (e.g. “shortest route using 500 m residential streets”), ox_route_pareto() enumerates full Pareto front cost-vs-preference trade-offs. run bicriteria label-setting solver (Martins’ algorithm) dominance pruning reverse-Dijkstra bounds Rust core — exact, deterministic, one-way streets respected. new helper ox_add_edge_penalties() builds penalty/resource edge column OSM highway classes; added onto routing weight also covers simple scalarized (“soft preference”) routing ox_shortest_path(). ox_route_constrained(method = "lagrangian") adds Lagrangian-relaxation solver (LARAC algorithm) beside exact one: budget constraint dualized iteration plain Dijkstra weight + lambda * resource, scales networks exact front grows large. route returned always feasible carries proven lower_bound optimal cost (cost == lower_bound certifies optimality; message reports duality gap). exact method now also reports lower_bound, always equal cost (#5). Route geometry reconstruction dramatically faster large graphs. bicriteria routers now receive traversed edge indices straight Rust solvers, parallel-edge lookup needed — geometry exact even across parallel edges differ cost resource (previously minimum-weight twin drawn). NCR Delhi drive network (1.0M nodes / 2.1M directed edges) ox_route_constrained() query runs ~0.7 s 9-route ox_route_pareto() front ~1.5 s, ~16 s ~140 s. ox_route_tsp(), parallel-edge lookup now built per call instead per leg (sorts numerically instead string key).

title: osmnxr 0.1.0
text: First public release OSMnx R. ox_example() loads small bundled real network (central Olinda, Brazil) examples vignettes show real analyses offline. vignettes reworked around real cases Boeing (2025) OSMnx examples gallery: multi-city orientation entropy (Chicago/New Orleans/Rome), betweenness chokepoints, travel-time routing isochrones, amenity accessibility. ox_orientation_entropy() ox_plot_orientation() now accept either osm_graph numeric vector bearings. ox_plot_figure_ground() draws figure-ground diagrams, ox_example() now also bundles "manhattan" "rome" networks new “Figure-ground diagrams” vignette (Boeing 2025, Fig. 3). ox_simplify() now preserves traversability per direction, emitting bidirectional edges two-way streets (fixes zero-valued routing/centrality simplified graphs). Download street networks OpenStreetMap (ox_graph_from_place(), ox_graph_from_address(), ox_graph_from_point(), ox_graph_from_bbox()) via Overpass API, returning tidy sf-backed osm_graph object. Geocoding Nominatim (ox_geocode(), ox_geocode_to_sf()). Rust compute core (via extendr): CSR graph, Dijkstra routing (ox_shortest_path(), ox_distances(), ox_nearest_nodes()) metrics (ox_basic_stats(), ox_bearings(), ox_orientation_entropy()). example_osm_graph() synthetic grid offline examples tests. Configuration via ox_settings() session caching ox_clear_cache(). Topology cleanup (Rust core): ox_simplify() merges chains interstitial degree-2 nodes single edges; ox_consolidate_intersections() merges nearby nodes one (via connected components); ox_nearest_edges() finds closest edge point. Advanced routing (Rust core): ox_k_shortest_paths() (Yen’s algorithm), ox_distance_matrix() (many--many), ox_isochrone() (reachable-area polygons via multi-source Dijkstra + concave hull). Travel-time routing: ox_add_edge_speeds() ox_add_edge_travel_times() add speed_kph / travel_time edge columns time-weighted shortest paths isochrones. New vignette: “Routing isochrones”. Network metrics (Rust core): ox_centrality() (betweenness via Brandes’ algorithm, closeness) ox_circuity() (street straightness). Circuity now also reported ox_basic_stats(). Interoperability: ox_as_sfnetwork(), ox_as_tidygraph() ox_as_dodgr() hand graph wider R network ecosystem. Export persistence: ox_to_geojson(), ox_to_maplibre() (style fragment), ox_save_graphml() / ox_load_graphml() lossless round-trip (edge geometry stored WKT), compatible OSMnx / NetworkX / Gephi. Feature downloads: ox_features_from_place() ox_features_from_bbox() fetch POIs, buildings amenities OpenStreetMap tidy sf points. ox_plot_orientation() draws polar rose plot street bearings (ggplot2). Documentation: vignettes “Urban metrics”, “Street orientation”, “Features points interest”, “Interoperability export” “Accessibility analysis”; full pkgdown reference articles menu.
